title: Bidirectional A*: the fastest way to stitch routes!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* search from both start and goal on real street graphs at once. It meets in the middle, dramatically shrinking the explored area while still using A* guidance for speed.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Noe Valley routes, but make them algorithmic.

Today’s visualization runs **Bidirectional A***: two A* searches launch simultaneously—one forward from your start node, the other backward from the destination. Each frontier uses the heuristic (e.g., straight-line distance mapped onto street distances) to prioritize promising intersections, while the two expanding wavefronts **converge at a meeting node**. ✅

🗺️ In graph terms: we model the real street map as a **weighted graph** (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges). Bidirectional search reduces the number of processed nodes by splitting the search effort, so you often explore far fewer streets than unidirectional A*—especially on large maps.

🚦 Want to see the pathfinding “handshake” in action? Hit **like**, save this reel, and comment **“NEAREST”** for my next heuristic idea! 👇
fb_caption:
Ever wondered how pathfinding can get faster without losing correctness? 🤖

We’re using **Bidirectional A*** on a real street graph: the algorithm runs A* from the start and the goal simultaneously, expanding two frontiers until they meet. This graph search strategy typically reduces explored nodes by dividing the work, while still using heuristic guidance to efficiently find the shortest route.

📌 Share this with a friend learning algorithms, and tell me: should the next video use time-dependent edge weights or turn costs?
yt_description:
San Francisco (Noe Valley) street-map pathfinding visualization with **Bidirectional A*** 🔥

In this YouTube Shorts clip, we model roads as a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, streets = edges) and run **Bidirectional A*** to search from start and goal at the same time. The two A* frontiers use a heuristic to prioritize promising paths, then meet in the middle for a shorter overall search.

Keywords: bidirectional a*, pathfinding, A* algorithm, graph search, shortest path, real map, coding visualization, CS algorithms

Watch to the end, then comment your favorite part: the convergence moment or the frontier expansion!
